title: JWST Over-Massive Early Galaxies
bottleneck: JWST found surprisingly massive, luminous galaxies at redshifts 10-14, earlier than standard galaxy formation expected, straining LambdaCDM's timeline for assembling stellar mass. Explanations range from bursty star formation and top-heavy IMFs to genuinely faster structure growth, with spectroscopic confirmations still catching up to photometric candidates. Some candidates turned out to be lower-redshift interlopers or active galactic nuclei, but a population of genuinely early massive systems persists.
why_it_blocks: If the abundance holds, either galaxy formation physics or the underlying cosmology needs revision at early times.
current_state: Spectroscopy has confirmed several z>10 galaxies but revised some masses downward; the tension is easing yet not resolved. Deeper spectroscopy and wider JWST surveys will determine whether galaxy formation models need modest tweaks or major revision.
